newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ABARE sees little problem with NZ apples.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ABARE sees little problem with NZ apples.

text.p: Australia's apple market would be minimally affected by New Zealand imports, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Thursday.
"Assuming that there were to be no disease incursion, the impact of apple imports from New Zealand would be minimal," ABARE's executive director Brian Fisher said in a statement.
Australia is considering lifting its current ban on fresh apple imports from New Zealand.
In a report on the possible economic impact, ABARE said Australia already competed on international markets and the impact of disease free apple imports was likely to be minimal.
But ABARE said a disease outbreak would cause production costs to rise, reduce competitiveness and could limit access to some markets.
A fruit disease called fire blight is present in New Zealand but not Australia.
Quarantine regulations currently prohibit imports of fresh apples although trade in processed apple products has been quite free, it said.
The Australian Quarantine and Inspection Service (AQIS) is studying the impact of lifting the ban and is due to report this year.

In its submission to the study, ABARE said the maximum total annual loss to producers of an outbreak of fire blight in all regions would be around 38 percent of the gross value of apple and pear production.
The gross value of Australian apple production in 1994/95 was A$269 million -- almost one percent of the total gross value of Australian agricultural production, ABARE said.
